plan.notes: SOURCE: '2025-2026 Old Dominion University Catalog — Bachelor of Science in Computer Science (w/ VCCS Equivalencies)', official ODU-hosted sample four-year curriculum, https://www.odu.edu/sites/default/files/2025/documents/2025-2026-vccs-computer-science-bscs.pdf (verified live 2026-09-30). TRANSCRIPTION: direct transcription of the document's 8-semester suggested ordering; VCCS equivalency columns omitted (Virginia community-college transfer mappings, not TCCNS). CATALOG YEAR: 2025-2026 is the most recent official term-by-term sequence found; no 2026-2027 edition was located as of 2026-09-30. Course titles/credits cross-checked against the live catalog requirements page (catalog.odu.edu/undergraduate/sciences/computer-science/computer-science-bscs/) and the official course list (catalog.odu.edu/courses/cs/): CS 251 = Programming with Java (4 cr), CS 260 = C++ for Programmers (1 cr), CS 315 = Computer Science Undergraduate Colloquium (1 cr), COMM 101R = Public Speaking, CS 121G = Introduction to Information Literacy and Research for Scientists, ENGL 231C = Introduction to Technical and Scientific Writing. CREDIT CAVEATS: the source PDF's own printed subtotals are internally inconsistent (e.g. Year 1 header says 32-33 but listed courses sum to 35 with Language and Culture; Junior Fall 13 only reconciles if CS 315 = 1 cr). This plan uses official catalog credit values throughout, which sum to exactly 120. 'Interpreting the Past' was placed in Fall Year 3 (the PDF's two-column layout is ambiguous in text extraction) because that placement reproduces the document's printed 13-credit Junior Fall subtotal. LANGUAGE AND CULTURE: the source lists 'Language and Culture I (may be waived)' in Fall Year 1 and 'Elective or Language and Culture II (may be waived)' in Spring Year 1. This plan includes both as student-choice slots, so the transcribed total is 123 credits — within the catalog's official 120-134 range. Students who waive Language and Culture substitute other electives to reach the 120-credit graduation minimum; the source PDF's printed year-total ranges are themselves internally inconsistent (e.g. Year 1 header 32-33 vs 32-35 from its own semester ranges) and are documented here as unreliable. PREREQUISITES: the sample plan gives a suggested ordering but states no explicit prerequisites, so prereq arrays are intentionally left empty rather than inferred; external_prereqs is therefore empty. CAVEAT: the current live catalog lists 'CS 422 or CS 480' as a required selection; the 2025-2026 sample plan covers it implicitly through the three 300/400-level CS elective slots (students should choose accordingly with an advisor). The source document states this plan is 'just one of several plans that will work' and students should consult an advisor and Degree Works.
